title: Money Treated as Having Reached the Rider Premium Account
content:
When arrears on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders are settled, what counts as money having reached the rider premium account depends on how the member's Medicare Advantage Health Plans bill stands — on the premium charges and premium payments booked on that enrollment's own premium account.

## The rule

**Where what has been paid on the medical plan bill is above the medical plan premium charged on it**, the money posted to the rider premium account is counted together with the money left over on the bill that is carried.

**Where the medical plan bill carries medical plan premium charged on it and what has been paid on it is not above that**, the shortfall on the bill is taken off the money posted to the rider premium account, the medical plan premium standing to be met first out of a combined payment.

**Otherwise**, only the money posted to the rider premium account is counted, no medical plan premium having been charged on the bill.

## The three cases set against one another

| What the medical plan bill shows | What counts as having reached the rider premium account |
|---|---|
| Paid above the medical plan premium charged | The money posted to the rider premium account, together with the money left over that is carried |
| Medical plan premium charged, and paid at or below it | The money posted to the rider premium account, less the shortfall on the bill |
| No medical plan premium charged on it at all | The money posted to the rider premium account alone |

## Worked on hypothetical inputs

Take money posted to the rider premium account of 20.00 USD.

- The medical plan bill shows 200.00 USD paid against 150.00 USD charged, and 30.00 USD of the money left over is carried. What counts as having reached the rider premium account is 20.00 USD together with 30.00 USD, that is 50.00 USD.
- The medical plan bill shows 120.00 USD paid against 150.00 USD charged. The shortfall is 30.00 USD, and what counts is 20.00 USD less 30.00 USD, which is never less than nothing: nothing.
- The medical plan bill shows 150.00 USD paid against 150.00 USD charged. What has been paid is not above what was charged, the shortfall is nothing, and what counts is 20.00 USD.
- The medical plan bill carries no medical plan premium charged on it. What counts is the 20.00 USD posted to the rider premium account alone.

Each figure is rounded to the nearest cent.
